questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Phase for the Amplitude-Phase Form for Sine
questions.problem: Given that the expression $2\operatorname{sin}⁡x+10\operatorname{cos}⁡x$ can be written as $R\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+ϕ)$ with ${0}^{∘}<ϕ<{90}^{∘}$ and $R>0$, what is the value of $ϕ?$
questions.worked_solution:
The sum formula for sine gives

$$
\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+ϕ) & =R(\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ) \\  & =R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡x+R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by writing the given expression in the amplitude-phase form

$$
2\operatorname{sin}⁡x+10\operatorname{cos}⁡x=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+ϕ),
$$

we get the following identity:

$$
2\operatorname{sin}⁡x+10\operatorname{cos}⁡x=(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{sin}⁡x+(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{cos}⁡x
$$

Equating the coefficients of $\operatorname{sin}⁡x$ and $\operatorname{cos}⁡x,$ we get the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ=2 \\ R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ=10\end{aligned}
$$

Dividing the second equation by the first, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}{R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ} & =\frac{10}{2} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡ϕ & =5 \\ ϕ & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(5).\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Amplitude-Phase Form for Sine
questions.worked_solution:
The difference formula for sine gives

$$
\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x-ϕ) & =R(\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ-\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ) \\  & =R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)-R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by writing the given expression in the amplitude-phase form

$$
2\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)-4\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x-ϕ),
$$

we get the following identity:

$$
2\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)-4\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)=(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)-(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)
$$

Equating the coefficients of $\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)$ and $\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x),$ we get the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ=2\sqrt{2} \\ R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ=4\end{aligned}
$$

Dividing the second equation by the first, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}{R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ} & =\frac{4}{2\sqrt{2}} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡ϕ & =\sqrt{2} \\ ϕ & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\sqrt{2}) \\  & =0.955\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places.

Now, we find the amplitude $R.$ Squaring the first and the second equations of the system and adding the results together, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)}^{2}+{(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)}^{2} & =(2\sqrt{2})^{2}+{4}^{2} \\ {R}^{2}({cos}^{2}⁡ϕ+{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ) & =8+16 \\ {R}^{2} & =24 \\ R & =2\sqrt{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we only consider the positive root since $R>0.$

Finally, we can write the initial expression in amplitude-phase form as follows:

$$
2\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)-4\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)=2\sqrt{6}\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x-0.955)
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Amplitude-Phase Form for Cosine
questions.worked_solution:
The difference formula for cosine gives

$$
\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-ϕ) & =R(\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ+\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ) \\  & =R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\operatorname{cos}⁡x+R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by writing the given expression in the amplitude-phase form

$$
2\operatorname{sin}⁡x+5\operatorname{cos}⁡x=R\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-ϕ),
$$

we get the following identity:

$$
2\operatorname{sin}⁡x+5\operatorname{cos}⁡x=(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{sin}⁡x+(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{cos}⁡x
$$

Equating the coefficients of $\operatorname{sin}⁡x$ and $\operatorname{cos}⁡x,$ we get the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ=2 \\ R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ=5\end{aligned}
$$

Squaring the first and the second equations of the system and adding the results together, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)}^{2}+{(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)}^{2} & =(2)^{2}+(5)^{2} \\ {R}^{2}({sin}^{2}⁡ϕ+{cos}^{2}⁡ϕ) & =4+25 \\ {R}^{2} & =29 \\ R & =\sqrt{29}\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we only consider the positive root since $R>0.$

$$

Therefore, by writing the given expression in the amplitude-phase form

$$
5\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)+2\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x+ϕ),
$$

we get the following identity:

$$
5\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)+2\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)=(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)+(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)
$$

Equating the coefficients of $\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)$ and $\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x),$ we get the following system of equations:

$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}{R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ} & =\frac{2}{5} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡ϕ & =\frac{2}{5} \\ ϕ & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{2}{5}).\end{aligned}

$5\operatorname{sin}⁡x-2\operatorname{cos}⁡x≈$

$\operatorname{sin}⁡(x\,-$
{{field-2}}$)$
questions.worked_solution:
The difference formula for sine gives

$$
\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-ϕ) & =R(\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ) \\  & =R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡x-R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by writing the given expression in the amplitude–phase form

$$
5\operatorname{sin}⁡x-2\operatorname{cos}⁡x=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-ϕ),
$$

we get the following identity:

$$
\begin{aligned}5\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(x) & =(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{sin}⁡x-(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{cos}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Equating coefficients, we obtain

$$
{\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ=5 \\ R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ=2\end{aligned}
$$

Dividing the second equation by the first:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}{R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ} & =\frac{2}{5} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡ϕ & =\frac{2}{5} \\ ϕ & =arctan\,(\frac{2}{5}) \\ ϕ & ≈0.381\,\text{rad},\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places.

For the amplitude,

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ+{R}^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡ϕ & ={2}^{2}+{5}^{2} \\ {R}^{2}({sin}^{2}⁡ϕ+{cos}^{2}⁡ϕ) & =4+25 \\ {R}^{2} & =29 \\ R & =\sqrt{29}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
5\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)≈\sqrt{29}sin\,(x-0.381).
$$
